episodes.title: We're Hot Rod People Now

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: After two recap segments catching up the table, the party (Argyle, Anzu, Benny, and Johnny — the band "Iconoclasm") spent their last night at the Sin and Tonic in Hallia sharing motives and backstory, were pulled into a dream-meeting with the god Aut in the Black and White, then set out by car for Ragnroost to join the strider pilgrimage toward the Voidsong — surviving a magical caltrop sabotage and a mercenary roadblock ambush along the way.

episodes.episodeTitle: Crying and Critting on a City with Legs

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: After finally swapping personal backstories at an inn, the party (Iconoclasm) drives to Ragged Roost, survives an ambush on the road, boards the colossal walking city-machine known as the Strider for a six-day pilgrimage, and plants their keystone — fighting off waves of "thought" creatures inside a void-space to birth their own heart, "Eerie," and construct the beginnings of a home aboard the Strider.

episodes.episodeTitle: The Delivery Truck for a Massacre

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

transcript.text: So at the bunker — the Scale's forward base, the concrete bunker with the sonar dish, camouflaged, they ride one of Chuck's floating discs over—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Gun barrel through the porthole.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —yeah, gun poked through the door's little window, just in case, very friendly — and Argyle's trying to ask them to look into his classified giant intel, and he keeps botching the scale of it, like he goes, look out for a ten-thousand-foot-tall red giant—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the GM keeps correcting him.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The GM has to feed him the real number mid-question, and Benny just deadpans, I don't think we'd have to look out for something that's ten thousand feet tall, it's pretty noticeable.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's pretty noticeable. Ha.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It'd be over the horizon.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And who'd they meet there — the sick kid—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Lance! Lance Vesper, the rifleman's Cassian, and Bishop, and Lance is — he looks awful, rheumy eyes, pale, and he goes, I am twenty-two—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You wouldn't believe it from my countenance.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —you wouldn't believe it from my countenance, and then he offers Argyle a refund if he can't cure him—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A refund. On the sickness.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the sickness might be a curse, that's the hook, nobody knows, which is why Argyle later swaps a feat to Break Curse just in case—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Wait but Lance is the one who said the clown thing—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Yes! Lance, blunt, goes, these clowns clearly have an ulterior motive or twelve—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Or twelve.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Smart kid. Sick, but smart.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I've been this size since I was zero days old.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's not — that's a different—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I know, I just like saying it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Food coming?

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I ordered the thing. The board thing.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay but back to Johnny because this is the part that breaks my heart a little—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Johnny and the Jets.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —so Johnny's whole plan, eventually, is to make the party look like harmless lucky bumblers, right, burns a performance check at the cookout to sell it, we're just idiots who got lucky—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Too late.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Way too late! Because Benny already went and flexed in the gym in front of two of the same orgs that are at the cookout! Bishop watched him read a fight! Paavo watched!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So the bumbler plan's dead on arrival.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Dead before he casts it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They saw the kid take a flat twenty-seven to scout a swordsman.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's not bumbling, that's casing the joint.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then on top of that Johnny burns Lie to Me on the MC—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh no.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —the one guy at the table who rolls a forty-three crit on deception—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Crit. Against the feat.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Crit against Lie to Me, learns absolutely nothing, the man is a sealed box, completely unreadable—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Okay so what is the point of Lie to Me, genuinely—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It works most of the time!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Does it though—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It works on people who aren't fiends.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So, not the important ones.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's — okay that's a little harsh but—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And — here, here's my note, and I will die on this—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh here we go.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Johnny is in a room with a being tied to a devil, who resonates with the Voidsong, the literal song his whole life is about—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Mm.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: —and what's the question Johnny doesn't ask. Same as always. He'll prod a fiend with a feat but he won't ask anybody why his own god stopped picking up the phone.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's not — that's not the same situation, Pip.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's exactly the same situation! There's a being right there that resonates with the song—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The MC denied being Illmari, though.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I'm not saying ask about Illmari—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Wait, he denied being Illmari? I thought—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Confirmed Illmari's alive. Said it's not my story to tell.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, right, not my story to tell, that was — okay yeah.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I'm saying there's a guy who hears the song and Johnny's instinct is to lie-detector him, not ask him anything real. It's the totaled car all over again—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The car was a tactical loss—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: THERE it is.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It was not.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It bought us time!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It bought you a wreck. You bet on the bet and the bet was bad.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We're hot rod people now, that's just who we are—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Build me a hood out of a box of scraps in a cave.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Exactly! That's the spirit!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You'll defend anything that's on fire.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I — okay that one's fair.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I'm telling you, Johnny's gonna take Aut's deal eventually. The oath's got a price, we just haven't hit it, and the day he can't ask his own god, Aut's gonna be right there with the toothy grin—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: You keep saying that—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And I'll be right.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: You bet on that the way I bet on the car.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's — okay that's actually a good one, I'll allow it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Recap, though. We skipped Benny's recap.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh god, the recap. Benny — wait, Benny did the recap? For the hero point?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Mike did. Benny's player.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, Mike did it, and the whole thing is supposedly just the facts, no embellishment, he arrives at the Strider, meets the orts—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The orts—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —the little — the orts, parks near Hildebrandt, plants the seed of inspiration, grows the heart, beats up monsters to power it, names the butler Chuck, names the heart—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Ear That Hears the Truth.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Ear That Hears the Truth, and then the GM goes, oh, funny thing, that's actually the name of a real mythic feat. Half the party has it.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Benny doesn't.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Benny named the heart, and Benny's the one guy who doesn't have the feat, so he gets none of the benefits—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You don't get the benefits even if they share the same name.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Even if they share the same name, direct quote, brutal.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Chuck the butler though. Offered any name in the world—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —picks Chuck.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Most boring possible. And the heart's named Eerie?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Eerie's the heart. Ear That Hears the Truth's the name.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Wait so it's both—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Eerie. That's the body. The name is the long one.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay. Sure. And Chuck's a cat.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Chuck's a cat?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Big, brown, just a cat. And he very passively accepted the name. Didn't want one. The figurine crumbles to dust, way more dust than a little figurine should have, and then Chuck hands you a replacement figurine—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I called it. Months ago. The eldritch hand-monster thing — I said whatever they drag out of the void's gonna get named Chuck.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That was a different Chuck.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's always Chuck! That's my point!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The barber's fake, though.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The — okay, see, this is the fight. Mike swears, no embellishment, just facts, and somewhere in the recap there's a barber on the Strider who only knows one haircut—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The flat top.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —only does flat tops, and the whole table goes, you made that up, that wasn't in the session, and Mike insists it's real—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It wasn't real.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and Argyle, Argyle defends him, not because he remembers the barber, just on principle—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: On principle alone—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —he goes, if Benny says there's a barber, there's a barber, and that's — that's so Argyle, good for the sake of good, even when the good thing is a haircut that doesn't exist.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The self-litigating lawyer takes the barber case pro bono.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Ha. Yeah.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: There's no barber.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We hear you, Maeve.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the eight legs! Eight legs on each side of the Strider—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That part's real.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: How is THAT the real part and the barber's fake—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The ship has legs. It doesn't have a one-haircut barber.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: This world's broken.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh — and the name, the group name, they finally landed on it. Chronicle.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Chronicle. Hm.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Before the GM even asked! He'd flagged he wants an in-world group name eventually, and they just settled on it on their own, which never happens with this group—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu suggested it last session.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Did he? I thought it was Argyle—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu. Last session.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Anzu, okay. And the alternatives got shot down, the Voice of the Few—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Voice of the Few sounds like a cult.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The GM said it makes you sound like tyrants at best—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You're everything Bernie Sanders would hate.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He said that? In a fantasy game?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He said that.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I love and fear that man.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Argyle's still pushing his name that puns on some character nobody met—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, half the party never even met the guy, and the GM keeps vetoing it, confusing and tyrant-coded—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Everything Argyle likes is tyrant-coded, have you noticed—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He just wants good for the sake of good, the tyranny's incidental—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's — yeah that's a sentence.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Board's here.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh thank god.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Don't eat the — wait, is anything on there a war hero—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's a cheese board, Bram.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I'm just saying, last time—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Don't eat the gingerbread house, it's a war hero.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That was one time and Johnny was the one who—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Johnny ate it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Johnny ate the war hero, yeah, not me.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Okay but the father line. We keep dodging it. The MC inspects Benny's permission slip—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, the chilling one.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: —and goes, give my regards to your father when you next speak to him.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Benny's father's Atum, which Anzu half-remembers, something archival at Belvedere—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Doesn't quite resolve into a face.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So the read is — and tell me I'm wrong — the read is one of these new organized devils might be Benny's other half.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: There's four of them, the new ones, the Harlequin's the one the MC's tied to, and then the Shackle—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Sigzilheit.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —Sig— that one, the Hooded, and the Loam.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And the devil knows Benny's dad. Personally enough to send regards.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A nine-year-old with a permission slip and a devil who knows his father.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Hand the baby a revolver. It's tradition.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A bowl of children's guns. As a treat.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the worst part, the part that actually got the table quiet, is Anzu's whole theory going in, right—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The cry for help.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —the Voidsong's a cry for help, the source is the vocalist, somebody singing, somebody we're maybe supposed to rescue—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And now—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and now we find out we're on a boat the devil's steering toward the void on purpose, and he wants everybody aboard to kill each other on the way, and whoever's left fights for it at the wall—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Nineteen orgs.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Nineteen-plus, and he says I'll be encouraging it, I'll get bored, I make a habit of not entering any kind of circle—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's the devil tell, right, the circle thing—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's the tell. Won't sing in a circle. And I have favorites, you don't want to be my favorite, but you might end up there anyway.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So Anzu thought they were going to save a singer—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and instead they're the delivery truck for a massacre.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They confirmed the heart's not subservient to him, at least.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, the consult-the-spirits ritual, their own heart's not on his leash, small mercy—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which Argyle then trades AWAY—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He swaps Consult the Spirits for Break Curse, because of Lance, the sickness thing—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the code word.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh the code word's the best part. Because they're scared of a devil-double—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A devil swapping in for Argyle, right, so they need a code word to tell which Argyle's the real Argyle—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Two Argyles AGAIN—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and the word they land on is guac.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Or "what would you eat with what's on his shoulder."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: What's on his shoulder—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Don't ask, it's an Argyle thing, but if you can answer what you'd eat with it, you're the real one.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: This is how people get radicalized.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I love and — yeah.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Red string board too.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The board! Argyle builds the whole It's Always Sunny red-string board, pins everything up—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Of course he does. The one guy who can't read a room builds the conspiracy wall.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And orders Blast Boots. Moderate Blast Boots. On the cowboy boots.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We're hot rod people now.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We're hot rod people now! See, that one fits!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: ...anyway.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Eat your cheese.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay but the door-to-door, real quick, the networking, because there's a whole bit where Benny keeps eyeing the biggest guy on the yard—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The yard. It's a prison yard to Benny.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —to jump first, prison-yard logic, find the biggest guy day one, and Anzu and the GM both going, no, allies beat corpses—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Tas Millet did open math at them.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh, Prime Meridian, the bean-counter, Tas Millet, does the cost-benefit out loud, to your face, and lands on, I'll do a two-way info link, not an alliance—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Dry. The road guys are always dry.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Transit nexus energy.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the dhampir just slams the door—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Necrolog guy. Smells like formaldehyde.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Gaspar, slams it, sends them to the Pale Lantern Society, very curt—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The radio people warning was Stoke, sort of.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The blind reverend, Walter Stoke, glass robes, practiced in politics, friendly but won't commit to anything—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Everyone fancy's a radio person eventually and the radio people are always evil. Write it down.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He's a priest, not a radio—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Write it down.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He's not on the radio.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Yet.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Tamara, the Protectorate one, the tile armor, she goes, we're friends so long as we're friends—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Don't do anything too shysty.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —don't do anything too shysty, yeah, which, coming from the people who wanted to wait for the heart to get fat before murdering it—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A little rich. Yeah.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They didn't tell anyone about Berth Four.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, Aut told them to unlock Berth Four's door and they just — kept that one to themselves—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: See, NOW you're listening to Aut—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's Argyle, not Johnny—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's gonna be Johnny in the end. I'm telling you.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: You bet the car money on that—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's not the car, it's a read, I read people—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You read people. You don't read facts.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: ...that's fair, actually.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: She got you.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: She gets one. There's no barber, fine, but she gets one wrong eventually—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Not tonight.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Anyway the gala's on departure day, the welcoming one, they've got a week, Argyle got them moved physically next to Hildebrandt on the clock thing—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The plot clock. Wait, who's at twelve—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I don't — that I actually don't know—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: We weren't told.

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: As the Strider prepares to depart on its pilgrimage toward the Voidsong, the crew of Iconoclasm spends a week making introductions to the other orgs aboard, recruiting allies into their skein network, before attending the departure gala — where the energy tithe demanded by the Master of Ceremonies wrings a weak attendee inside-out and unleashes a swarm of monsters.

episodes.title: Twelve Seconds in the Inverted Ballroom
episodes.episodeTitle: Twelve Seconds in the Inverted Ballroom

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: Aboard the Strider as it begins jumping voidward along the horizon, the party survives the gala turning into a slaughter when a failed tithe rips open a void portal disgorging barghests and Ki-Rin onto the dance floor. After fighting through the carnage alongside rival factions, they brave the collapsing void-pocket beyond the portal to extract a chitinous "Voidheart" orb, dragging both their downed comrades and a Giant hand-creature back into real space.

episodes.title: Just Us, Dressed Up Nice

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: In the immediate aftermath of their excursion into the void portal at the gala, the party fends off the Hand of the Void abomination they dragged back, then loots the dead Garrick Textiles Fane, kills its heart, and feeds the spoils into their own heart-base — investing in a Siphon Array. They check on the unresponsive Protectorate (a false alarm), then convene a multi-faction alliance summit to negotiate excursions, mergers, and how to survive the escalating nine-day tithes aboard the Strider.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Fickle little man.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So combat's over, everybody heals up, and Argyle pulls Bishop aside, quietly, tells him Grayson was dominating a monster to make it attack people earlier in the night.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Bishop's like, cool, can't do anything with that.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Pretty much, he goes, there's no evidence, it'll be — what'd he say—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "Difficult to litigate in terms of public opinion."

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So what do we GAIN from snitching with no proof, that's my — like now Bishop just thinks you're paranoid.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: No, it's on the record now, it's in allied hands—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's in allied hands and unactionable. That's just gossip with a clipboard.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's "be on your guard."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's all it is.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And meanwhile Johnny's just standing there bleeding from the eyes and the nose, dried blood everywhere from the portal, like nobody's checked on him—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Nobody. The man's hemorrhaging and they're doing politics.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the totem — the keystone totem updates as the portal shrinks, because the Voidheart's out now, and it reads, uh — nine days till the next tithe, cost is twenty-one, energy eighty.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Cost twenty-one. Energy eighty.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And nine days is the clock.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Every nine days. Pay or the faction dies.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Cheerful little ship.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So then we — okay, we drive out to loot the Garrick place before Grayson can, the textiles one—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Garrick Textiles Fane.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Garrick Textiles, the fabric one, it's a Concordia thing, and we get there and it's already crumbling, falling apart, and there's no fabric inside—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The fabric's in the truck out back.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's all loaded in an eighteen-wheeler out back, yeah, and inside is the dying heart, the — Whirling in Rags.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Great name.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Josh, after the giant-hand thing, goes — "from now on I have to give hearts shorter names because I can't have you all calling it something-glove."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Something Glove. That's its band name now.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's never Chuck either. They never name them Chuck when they should.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's ALWAYS Chuck, that's the problem — anything we drag out the void ends up a Chuck.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: This one we didn't get to name, we killed it. So they send in Johnny and Benny to "gently speak to the heart"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The two highest kill counts.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The two with the highest kill count, sent in to negotiate gently.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's — okay that's the joke of the whole night. "Go talk it down." It's Johnny and Benny. They do not talk things down.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the heart goes, "I am aware that all of my contractors are dead. So not good."

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "So not good."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Reading the room better than the party.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And there was a whole debate, Benny wanted to ask it to go willingly, like surrender, and Argyle's just—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Rip it out and dip.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Rip it out and dip, yeah.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Of course. Of course Argyle wants the clean kill, but he'll feel TERRIBLE about it after for legal reasons—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Pro bono guilt.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Pro bono guilt, exactly.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So Johnny does double-speak, diversion, and Benny does a thievery check — thirty-six—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Thirty-six.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and plucks the core thread out like a little ball of yarn, and the heart dies instantly, and the whole Fane comes down, and everyone makes their reflex save to get out.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And we got, what, nothing for it?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Ten energy. Because Garrick couldn't even afford its own tithe.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Half energy for a kill. And it was a small heart.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So we learned the rules at least — kill, leave, or claim.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Kill's half. Claim's full but you have to defend it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, and killing it from inside collapses the building, that's the new rule.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That tracks.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So then we haul the eighteen-wheeler of fabric all the way home, to the Strider undercroft, the base—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We're hot rod people now.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We're hot rod people now! And we get into the long economy bit, the heart-feeding bit, this is — Argyle's whole — okay so first we feed the little Garrick core into Eerie, our heart—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Eerie.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Eerie says the line, "I have no allegiance to others of my kind, my only allegiance is to you," very loyal, very ominous.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: For now.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: For now.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's a heart. They're all somebody's heart eventually.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then it's just — Argyle's dumping EVERYTHING in, just gleefully, he's going "no guys, I want it to go high, I want to buy something BIG"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Spreadsheet brain.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Anzu's doing his bit, the whole — don't bank too much energy or he's gonna be like one of those flies rubbing its little hands together—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The fly. Rubbing the hands.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The more you put in, the more he can steal from you.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's the real concern, right, Anzu's actually making a point under the bit—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He is, but Argyle doesn't hear it because he's busy throwing in — what was the list — a pickled demon tongue, the gingerbread house—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: NO. The gingerbread house is a war hero, you do not—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We didn't eat it, we fed it to the heart—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's WORSE—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A choker of elocution, a Symbol of Conflict, a crushing rune, the fortifying pebble, barghest fur, Ki-Rin blood—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the demon tongue. Pickled.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the demon tongue, yeah.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Johnny was gonna eat that gingerbread house, I know it. He was eyeing it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The rate's one energy per ten gold on magic items, that's the precedent now.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: One per ten.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the big buy is the Siphon Array, costs forty, but it gives plus two energy on every future sacrifice forever, so it compounds—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So Argyle gets his big purchase.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He gets his big thing! And the other clever bit — the Voidheart, it's worth like forty energy if you feed the whole thing, or twenty if you keep part of it intact, and it's a magic-dampening item, so they feed in HALF and keep half to seed a future magic-negation project—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Against Grayson.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Against Grayson and his thirty-five DCs, exactly, you want a way to shut his magic down later.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Okay that's — that's actually smart. Half now, half toward dampening the radio guy. Who came up with that, that's not an Argyle plan.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It was sort of a group—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's too patient for Argyle.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Yeah. Yeah, that's Anzu.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the Siphon Array purchase comes with — they get a G-Wagon out of it, so now we're building a garage—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A garage.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A multi-purpose garage for the G-Wagon, and Argyle wants — oh, this is the head, the Ki-Rin head—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The butterfly! Benny parried the hoof with a butterfly!

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: With a butterfly, yeah, an actual butterfly—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Not a sword.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Not a butterfly SWORD, that ruins it, just a butterfly. The little insect.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So Argyle wants the Ki-Rin head mounted over the front door of the base, as a trophy—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Of course he does.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and it's not preserved, it's just a raw elk-deer head, and he asks the twins, the — Anouk and Anaïs—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anouk and Anaïs.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —to preserve it, but Anzu keeps going, every time, "this thing has not been properly preserved, this is disgusting."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Johnny's like it's gonna be a rotting head!

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "It's gonna be a rotting head," yeah.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So Argyle wants — what's his reasoning, he wants people to "just see the head"?

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: People walk by, they just see the head.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Everything Argyle likes is tyrant-coded. Mounting a rotting head over your door so the peasants see it on the way to work, that's — that's a guy with a head problem.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And we're right next to the nervous rival factions, that's the thing, we're trying to be low-profile and we've got a spy tower, an eighteen-wheeler in the yard, and a rotting elk head—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Low profile.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Johnny does the whole rumor-mill bit, he goes, "those four guys jumped into the magic hole, came out with a giant hand thing, and then walked away. No explanation."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's exactly what it looks like, though. That's just what happened.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That IS what happened.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We are the rumor.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So then — okay, we invite all the allied factions over for a debrief, and the Protectorate doesn't respond, and Prime Meridian says they're not coming in person—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: PM declined.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: PM declined, and so the party gets paranoid, cancels the whole meeting they themselves called, and drives across the entire Strider in the middle of the night to do a wellness check on the Protectorate—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Why.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Because they got nervous!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: No but — wait, the door thing. Berth four. Aut's whole — the unlock-the-door errand.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "Sussy birth four," Benny said.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Sussy berth four.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's tangled up in it, maybe.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's the real why, isn't it. They're not actually worried about the Protectorate, they've got this secret Aut job rattling around—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Maybe, the GM never said—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The oath has a price they haven't found yet. I keep saying it. Johnny takes Aut's deal in the end.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: You keep saying it.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And I'll be right.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So we drive ALL the way over, Johnny does the talking, in sunglasses, at night—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: At night.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: At night, and the guard out front just says yeah, Yao and Tamara are fine, they're recovering, not taking visitors, and the sense-motive rolls confirm he's not lying.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He's telling the truth.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He's telling the truth, so it was all for nothing, and Ichel goes, "that's it? we drove over here so you could talk to the security guard out front?"

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Brutal.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the GM as Ichel, "we're kind of just along for the entertainment at this point."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I mean—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Argyle keeps going, on repeat, "checking on our comrade really isn't that crazy," "it's good diplomacy"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It is a little crazy, though.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's a tactical loss—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: NO. No, see, that's — that's exactly the totaled car all over again. "Tactical loss." That was a paranoid midnight road trip, Bram, that's not diplomacy—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's good to check on your—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: You called the meeting! YOU called it and then drove away from it to go stare at a guard booth! Your guy can't read a room, that's the—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He reads the room, he just—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He litigates it.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He litigates the room.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Fine, fine. So the next morning, the real summit, everyone — some in person, PM and the Protectorate dialing in remote—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Radio people.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and Johnny gives the debrief and rolls low on diplomacy, so everyone thinks we're hiding something—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the reroll.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh the reroll! He mythic-rerolls the bad roll and gets ANOTHER natural one.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A double nat one.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Two.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's the curse. That's the inverted curse. A thirty-four knows nothing and a one knows — a one knows even less, somehow—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The man is cursed.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He's so cursed. Ghosted by his god, twice-nat-one'd, bleeding from the eyes—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So because the debrief tanks, everyone's suspicious, and that's when the real math comes out — Mr. Flock points out the tithe ticked up to twenty-one—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which means a shared pot.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A shared pot, about four hundred total, split across all the factions, so — here's the brutal part — as factions die, the tithe goes UP for everyone left.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh that's nasty.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's nasty. So keeping the weak ones alive lowers your own bill.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: But the vultures—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The vultures converge on the falling ones.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Tas, from Prime Meridian, just says the quiet part — "it is obvious to me that at some point we will have to consider cutting away some members of the flock."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Just says it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Flat.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: While the party's tiptoeing around it, Tas just — names it. Who gets cut.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then Salvado, from Solari, the little shipping one, who's basically next on the chopping block, goes, "you guys, you wouldn't let me die, right?"

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh, Salvado.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Salvado.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: That's — okay that's the gut-punch line of the night, that's worse than any of the combat.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Argyle, the WHOLE time, is just furiously doing four-hundred-divided-by-faction-count math in his head—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Spreadsheet brain. Of course. Everyone's having a moment and he's doing long division.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Kadou offers to build a magic-item detector if we give him a map, Paavo offers to scout ahead—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Paavo scouts.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and the travel math is wild, the journey to the wall is like four and a half months, fifteen cycles—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: One void per six seconds.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: One void every six seconds, and you can fall like forty-eight hours behind the Strider and still catch up.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And the only place to get fresh magic items is the — what, the Joker Worlds?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Excursions to the Joker Worlds. Yeah.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, that's the only source.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I was — I thought the items came from the hearts.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Huh. Okay.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So then it's all negotiation to close out — the party pitches a faction merger, to share the tithe burden, and PM refuses to pool magic items—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: PM won't pool items.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: PM won't pool, but they'll let us pay their tithe increase, and then we agree to absorb the two weak non-combat ones — Solari and Alkahest—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So we DID save Salvado.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We saved Salvado!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Good. Good. He asked so nicely.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We take in their people, take their hearts — Solari's heart is twenty energy, Alkahest's is thirty—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And claiming nets about twenty-five.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —nets us about twenty-five, and we cede the empty territory over to the Protectorate, and we needle Radiant Arms—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Y'shael.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Y'shael, into joining as a forward buffer base, the gun people—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "Just a tap'll do ya."

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "Just a tap'll do ya," yeah, and Johnny rolls a thirty-five diplomacy to seal Radiant Arms and Ichel coming in—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Thirty-five. Finally.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Off the double nat one to a thirty-five. The curse breaks at the worst possible — no, the best possible time.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Bishop says the nice thing, he goes, "you don't need to pay our tithe, we're fine paying the increase if it means you're keeping other groups safe, because they'd die otherwise."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Aw.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Benny's whole take is, give them the full tithe anyway, even though we know they'd accept less, just to stay in their good graces—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: See but is that shrewd or is that just Argyle's spreadsheet talking us into bankrolling the entire ship—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's coalition-building—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's "just us." It's not justice, it's "just us," dressed up nice—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's generous!

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's generous with the whole party's money, sure. We're now paying — what, PM's offset, Hildebrandt's offset—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Hildebrandt and Prime Meridian, yeah.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We're paying for everybody. That's not an alliance, that's an allowance. Argyle's just adopted the entire flock.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We're the hub now! We went from one faction to the center of the whole—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: We're the hub that pays everyone's bills. That's — that's not a hub, that's a—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It locks in the coalition against Grayson's bloc, that's the point—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: At what recurring cost though, that's all I'm—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A higher recurring tithe that we've pledged to offset, yes, but—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "But." There's the but.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It pays off if nobody falls.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And somebody always falls. Tas said so.

episodes.title: The Canary in the Ballroom

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: Over a month aboard the colossal walking city-machine the Strider, the band Iconoclasm goes from blowing up a city block in Hallia to becoming the political and military hub of a pilgrimage toward the Voidsong: they finally bare their backstories to one another, refuse a god's bargain on the road, board the Strider and birth their own heart "Eerie," then learn the pilgrimage is a devil-hosted death game powered by a lethal energy tithe — culminating in a gala massacre, a harrowing dive into a collapsing void-pocket for a Voidheart, and a coalition summit where they remake themselves as the alliance that keeps the weak factions alive.
