transcript.text: The battletrance thing—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Yao's will save spared only Argyle. Vaporized three others.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Bishop, the lizard, drops a hundred-foot Storm of Battle—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Argyle FLIPS—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Instantly! He was all "the Protectorate are so cool" and the second Bishop's lightning goes off it's "no, the SCALE are the cool ones"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Fickle little man. Whoever did the last cool thing. No loyalty.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Grayson — Master Grayson — casts a modified Dominate and just TAKES a Ki-Rin—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Silven Grayson.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which is a hostile move, right, that's him showing his hand—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A guy hijacking a monster mid-fight, yeah, and the party scrambles to publicize that, like, hey everyone, see what HE just did—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Anzu's Mindbird cleaned up.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Anzu's Mindbird, mental and sonic magic, just racking up kills, and every time he snipes a kill off Benny—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "Mindbird claims another."

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "Mindbird claims another," Benny lines one up and Anzu just steals it—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Benny's crying, losing kills, cursed, it's not his night.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He critted in melee though.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He did keep critting. Weeping and critting.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then there's the portal, the void portal in the middle of the floor that's just—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu figured it out. Self-closing fracture.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, it's not a designed door, it's a — the tithe ripped the energy out so violently it tore the weave, so the whole ship's fabric of magic is weakened now and portals could pop open ANYWHERE—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which is the scary worldbuilding part, that's a structural problem now, not a one-off—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Othello scouts through—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The raven.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Normal raven.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Just a regular-sized raven, and beyond the portal it's this inverted ballroom, hands pushing through the walls like the walls are elastic, and floating up top is a — a purple chitinous orb, the Voidheart, over a giant HAND pulled out of the ground—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And the hand things echolocate—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Echolocating hand-masses, and Othello takes twenty void damage just scouting and bails—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Bishop reads it. "Somebody designed this to cause conflict."

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "This is right fucked," he goes, "somebody designed this to cause conflict amongst us," because as factions die the tithe goes UP on everyone left—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And there's a wall, way out, past void one-point-four million, that nobody comes back from—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: One-point-four million. No one returns.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And before that — the skinning, oh—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Lance.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Lance, this guy, skins EVERYTHING, habitually skins everything, and Johnny gets roped into skinning the barghests, and Johnny had the worse survival skill, and Argyle made HIM do it anyway—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Why—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "Because I thought it'd be funny."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Because he thought it'd be funny. That's the whole reason. Made the worse skinner do the gross skinning for a laugh—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Argyle hacks a Ki-Rin head off as a trophy, which — remember that, that head matters later—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The rotting head.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then the dive, the Voidheart dive, this is the climax — they decide to grab the Voidheart before the portal seals, so they stack everything on Benny, Godspeed, silence, guidance, and shoot him in—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Eighty-five feet. Crit-grabs the orb.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Sprints eighty-five feet and crit-grabs it, and the silence works because—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The hands echolocate, so silence blinds them—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Right.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the second he pulls the orb, the whole place COLLAPSES, temperature plummets, hands burst out of the walls everywhere, and these — the hands, the real stat block, it reads—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Reach one thousand.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Reach one THOUSAND feet, it's a reskinned something, and they start battering the party, Benny goes down, dying, Argyle goes down—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Benny goes super saiyan first—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh right, Benny — his hair, he's already blonde and the hair just gets LONGER—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Super saiyan Benny, the little android—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And dying, before he drops, he SHOVES Johnny and Anzu through the portal to safety, and then those two dive back IN to drag the bodies out one at a time—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: One at a time.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Anzu's last act is a Gravity Well crit that pulls himself AND the dropped Voidheart through right as the space implodes—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Argyle lives on a nat twenty death save—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Nat twenty. Burned his last hero point to stabilize.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Nat twenty death save and his last hero point, and Josh goes, "the whole thing took twelve seconds."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Twelve seconds. All of that.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they drag a whole giant hand-creature OUT with them into real space—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which — and this is the debrief argument — did the whole party even need to go in? Because Argyle's whole thing after was "we definitely shouldn't have followed Benny"—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Benny could've soloed it—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Benny stacked with Godspeed and silence could've grabbed it and run, and instead three more of them piled in and nearly all died—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But then the hand wouldn't've—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It worked out, I know, I know—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It nearly didn't.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But it DID, and then they've got to kill the hand they dragged out—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Ralph crit it. Holy spear.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Bishop crits with a holy spear, forty-eight damage, and that reveals it's weak to holy, suppresses the regeneration—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Grayson—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Grayson pointedly does NOT catch Argyle in his — his Vampiric Exsanguination cone, which is a level six, seven spell, save DC—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Thirty-five.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Thirty-five, which is "much scarier than level six," and he deliberately aims it so it misses Argyle, to keep his cover as the innocent little healthcare worker—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So Argyle just standing there holding the Voidheart in the open, betting Grayson won't blow his cover—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the bet pays off—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The bet pays off because the DICE said so, that's not Argyle being smart, that's—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's reading the guy! He read that Grayson wants his cover more than he wants—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It was a gamble.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It was a gamble that happened to land.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And there's Lance's sniper stat block that literally just reads "Jaws," with a chomping—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: A little chomping animation, Josh—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Benny clutch rerolls a crit-fail into a crit-success on a will save against being dominated, hero point—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Crit fail to crit success.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then Grayson reaches for a scroll, like he's gonna raise the hand's corpse as an undead minion, and Argyle—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Bone Shaker.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "Yeah, I'm gonna bone shake him," and he chucks the whole corpse into the void so Grayson can't have it, and Grayson just — quietly pockets the scroll—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Slow-burn villain, that guy. He's gonna be the one.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He's the one.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And THEN — they're not done, they drive over to Obratz's ruined Fane to loot it before Grayson can—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Garrick Textiles—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the heart's still there, Whirling in Rags, still lucid, knows it's been abandoned—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "I am aware that all of my contractors are dead. So not good."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "So not good." Oof.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Benny wants to talk it into surrendering, like, go willingly—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Argyle just wants to rip it out and dip—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So they send in — and this is the joke — they send in "the two with the highest kill count" to "gently speak to the heart"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The two most violent guys, to negotiate gently—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Benny ripped out its core thread.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Benny just — thievery check, thirty-six, plucks the core like a little ball of yarn, kills it instantly—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So much for going willingly—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And killing a heart inside its Fane collapses the Fane, so the building comes down and everyone makes their reflex save out, and they got — what, ten energy—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: About ten. Garrick couldn't pay the tithe, so there was barely anything left.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: All that for ten. The fabric was in the truck out back anyway—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Josh goes, "from now on I think I have to give hearts shorter names"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Whirling in Rags, yeah, that's a mouthful when it's dying—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And THEN the economy session—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh, the spreadsheet—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They haul this stolen eighteen-wheeler of fabric back and they start feeding stuff into Eerie, like, a pickled demon tongue, the gingerbread house—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: They fed the war hero to Eerie?!

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They fed the gingerbread house—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I thought Johnny was gonna eat it—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Into Eerie. And a choker of elocution, a crushing rune, barghest fur, Ki-Rin blood—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they analyze the Voidheart and it's a magic-dampening item, so they feed in HALF of it to seed a magic-negation project for later—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Against Grayson's big scary spells, right, the DC thirty-five stuff—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, and they buy a Siphon Array, plus two energy on every future sacrifice, and Argyle is GIDDY—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "I want it to go high! I want to buy something big!"

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: "No, guys, I want it to go HIGH, I want to buy something big," and Anzu's the brakes, Anzu's like, don't bank too much—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "He's going to be like one of those flies." Rubbing its hands.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The fly rubbing its little hands—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Because the more you feed Eerie the more he can steal from you, Anzu doesn't trust—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Eerie's whole pitch is—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "I have no allegiance to others of my kind. My only allegiance is to you."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which is either very reassuring or the most ominous thing—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then the HEAD—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The rotting head—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Argyle insists on mounting the Ki-Rin head over the front door, the unpreserved one, the rotting one—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "This thing has not been properly preserved. This is disgusting."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Anzu just keeps saying it, "this is disgusting, this has not been preserved"—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they're trying to LAY LOW, that's the thing, they've got a spy tower and an eighteen-wheeler and now a rotting elk head over the door—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: They're the loudest, weirdest base on the boat and they're like, why's everyone nervous around us—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Benny's meme about it, the Voidheart hanging out with Eerie—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "The dog is the only one that realizes it's a fucking bobcat."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The bobcat in the dog photo, yeah—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then they get PARANOID — the Protectorate doesn't answer, Prime Meridian won't come in person—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So they cancel their own meeting—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Cancel their own debrief and drive across the whole Strider at midnight for a "wellness check" on the Protectorate bunker—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Possibly tangled up with the Aut thing, the unlock-the-door thing—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "Birth four." Benny called it "sussy birth four."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "Sussy birth four"—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they get there and the compound's totally fine, and the guard just tells them, truthfully, Yao and Tamara are recovering, they're fine, not taking visitors—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And they dragged the Scale allies along—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Ichel and Bishop. Unimpressed.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Ichel goes, "that's it? We drove all the way over so you could talk to the security guard out front?"

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: And Josh as Ichel, "we're kind of just along for the entertainment at this point"—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Johnny does the talking in sunglasses. At night.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Sunglasses at night, of course. And Argyle's defensive the whole time, "checking on our comrade isn't that crazy"—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He said it like four times.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which is what you say when it IS that crazy—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Was it crazy though? Checking on your ally after a—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: You called the meeting! You summoned everyone and then ghosted your own meeting to go bother a security guard at midnight—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: ...okay it was a little crazy.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But then the summit, the real one, the alliance summit—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: This is where it all comes together.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The whole alliance convenes and they finally do the math out loud, the tithe is one shared pot, like four hundred—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Roughly four hundred. Split among all the factions.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Split among everyone, so as factions DIE the tithe per group goes UP—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: So everyone's death makes the survivors' bills worse—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Tas, Prime Meridian, just says the quiet part—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "At some point we will have to consider cutting away some of the members of the flock."

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Just says it. To everyone's faces—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Salvado, the little dwarf, who's right on the chopping block—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: "You guys, you wouldn't let me die, right?"

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Oh, that's brutal, the one honest guy on the boat going "you wouldn't let me die, right?"—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they DON'T! That's the turn — the party agrees to absorb the two factions most likely to die, Solari and Alkahest—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: For about twenty-five energy from their hearts.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They take in the underdogs, they cede some territory to the Protectorate, they recruit Radiant Arms as a buffer base, and they pledge to cover the tithe offsets for Prime Meridian AND Hildebrandt—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Which is where I go, is that shrewd or did Argyle's spreadsheet brain just sign them up to bankroll the entire ship—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's coalition-building! They become the HUB, they keep the weak factions alive, that's the whole—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: At the cost of a permanently higher tithe they swore to pay forever—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Bishop wouldn't take it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right — Bishop goes, "you don't need to pay our tithe, we're fine paying the increase if it means you're keeping other groups safe, because they'd die otherwise"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: See and THAT'S the moment Argyle should've worried the Scale are evil, because they're being nice—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's the good guys, though—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Nobody's that nice on a murder boat—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Probably good guys.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "Probably."

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they went from this one reckless band that blew up a city block in Hallia to the — the thing that holds the whole alliance together, the hub, against Grayson, four and a half months out to the wall—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: About fifteen cycles. One void per six seconds.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Fifteen cycles to the wall, and Johnny — oh, Johnny's roll on the debrief—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The double nat one—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He mythic rerolls a nat one and rolls ANOTHER nat one—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Two in a row.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: The man's god really has stopped picking up.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Which is the curse, the cursed dice, the whole — and he STILL won't ask Aut the question—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He STILL won't—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And I'm telling you, when the oath's price comes due, he signs—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: You've said that—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And I'll say it next week too—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: We'll see.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I just want to know WHY he won't ask. That's all I — like the god ghosted him and he's protecting the god's feelings—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: You... you kind of had to be there for that one—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I WAS there—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I know, I just—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Jorge's gonna recap it wrong anyway.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Oh, Jorge's recap is gonna be a disaster—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: Immediately wrong, the first sentence—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Immediately wrong, "last session the party went to the gym"—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: "—and named a dwarf"—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He'll skip the dishrag entirely.

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: He always skips the part that mattered—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Anyway, the bobcat. In the dog photo. That's — that's the heart and the Voidheart, that's—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: I get it, yeah—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's a good meme—

transcript.speaker: C
transcript.name: Pip
transcript.text: It's fine—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's better than fine, it's—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's fine.

episodes.title: A Big Juicy Heart

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm, unhurried, precise but terse; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Speaks the least and lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for; her power is the deadpan beat and the flat one-line correction, NOT the paragraph — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. The only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle. Grounds events in how the world actually works and reins Bram in when he embellishes

C.name: Pip
C.persona: quick, fond, incorrigible, fast but scattered; the needler who cares more about WHY the characters did the thing than what they did. Talks in fragments and questions, interrupts himself, free-associates sideways into tangents that go nowhere and deflate, and rarely sticks the landing on a thought; right about people, wrong about facts, and won't fully admit either. Second-guesses the table's heroics, pokes at sentiment with a wink, and goads the others into defending their takes — without waiting for his own point to finish

episodes.synopsis: After their meeting of the minds, the party hunts for a route-map of the Strider's path ahead — tracking it to the silent Harlequins' theatrical front-town and Curator Ocelith's library, where they learn the cosmology of the four Princes and the awakening eye and accept a quest to recover Ocelith's stolen ink ribbon from Subdeck 12. Along the way they fail to recruit Verdant Holdings, gather repeated warnings about Hildebrandt and Grayson's rival alliance, then under cover of night consume the hearts of their two newest small-faction allies for energy and fortify their base with walls, a moat, and a honeycomb maze design.

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm and dry, precise but pointed; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for and reins Bram in with a flat one-line correction — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. But she's not only the fact-checker: she needles, too, pushing on WHY the characters did what they did and making Bram defend his reads, poking at the table's heroics and at sentiment with a wink. Grounds events in how the world actually works; the only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle

episodes.synopsis: The party descends into the Undercroft of the Strider for the first time, discovering a hidden society of mutated mongrelfolk workers trapped in debt bondage to Harlequins. Following directions from a bird-like worker named Marin, they push into a forsaken sector where deeply mutated creatures worship one of the Sinister Six, wearing horn talismans and speaking an evolved dialect of the dead language Urthram. After a fierce battle against the unholy mongrelfolk, the party recovers the ink ribbon they were sent to find, discovers incomplete spell manuscripts titled 'Perfection's First Step,' and realizes the Sinister Six are emulating voidsong — before crossing the threshold into a Fane, where the session ends on a cliffhanger.

transcript.text: That's the Strider walking. That's what a strider does. It moves.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But feeling it from inside, from below, in this rickety elevator — the groaning, the creaking, it hasn't been used much — that's atmosphere. That's the GM earning his keep.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The GM also said floor nine before the players corrected him to twelve.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He forgot what numbers are! He said it himself!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He forgot what numbers are. Which is either charming or concerning depending on how much you trust your GM's prep.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I trust it. The vibe was there. And then Argyle — Argyle goes off on this numerology thing and I am HERE for it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Oh God.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He rolls a thirty-four religion and a thirty-six occultism —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Both excellent rolls, yes.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Both excellent! And the GM reveals — six outer gods, six other gods appearing, four princes — but no pervasive magic number. And Argyle just goes, fifteen floors, four hands plus one eye, times three, equals the princes times the hearts, and it's just — it's right in their faces, guys!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The GM explicitly said Argyle would think the fifteen connection is a stretch.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The GM said that! But Argyle pushes it anyway!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Because Argyle pushes everything anyway. Look — a thirty-four religion and a thirty-six occultism are great rolls. The lore he got is real. Six outer gods, six other gods, four princes — that's genuine cosmological information. But the numerology, the four plus one times three thing — that's pattern-matching, not pattern-finding. He's seeing faces in clouds.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Or he's seeing a real pattern that the GM planted and the in-character disclaimer is just the GM covering for the fact that Argyle stumbled onto something.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That's possible. I'll concede it's possible. But you don't get to assert it's true just because it'd be cool if it were. Fifteen floors could just be fifteen floors.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: In this game? Nothing is just anything. Everything means something.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That's a nice t-shirt. Let me know when it's a theory.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay, fine — but then the rust thing. The crafting check, a twenty-seven, reveals rust on the supposedly new Strider construction. Rust! On a new vehicle! Why would somebody build a new vehicle out of rusty metal?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Anzu says —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Anzu says they bought a used Strider and did some adjustments.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is either brilliant or the GM's worst nightmare of players reading too much into set dressing.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I think it's brilliant. I think it's the players engaging with the world as a real place. The Strider is supposedly new, it's got rust, the society checks don't tell them much about the strider market or Istria —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Hildebrandt mentioned a group that explored toward the wall. They were Istrian, didn't use a strider.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right, so there's this whole Istrian context they don't have access to yet, and the rust is a thread. It's a thread hanging there. And Anzu just —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu just grabbed it. Which I respect. But the society checks were a nineteen and a twenty-three. They failed to get meaningful information. So the theory is built on a critical crafting check and vibes.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Better than nothing.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: marginally.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So they open the bulkhead door into the Undercroft proper. Cramped hallways — seven feet across, six feet tall. Taller characters ducking. White panels with harsh light, not warm. And they hear a sea shanty. Off-key, many distinct voices, not harmonic. People working, somewhere deeper in.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Johnny starts whistling Wellerman.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I mean —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: While approaching underground workers who live in debt bondage beneath his feet. The GM notes this is like whistling about the tax man to people who live beneath you.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's Johnny! That's Johnny! He doesn't think about it, he just — the man heard a shanty and he whistled along. Is it tactless? Absolutely. Is it in character? One hundred percent.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's both. That's what makes it good. But then they find the workers and the whole tone shifts.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Yeah. About fifteen mutated humanoids maintaining lubricant platforms for the Strider's legs. A human with a third arm growing from his neck. An elf with peeling scales. A dwarf with one huge foot and one tiny foot. And Anzu's occultism — a thirty-five —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Identifies them as mongrelfolk. Slip-affected humanoids, mutated by unprotected large jumps on the slip. The condition is irreversible and isolating.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Irreversible. That word does a lot of heavy lifting.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It does. And Argyle immediately connects them to the minions the Harlequins summoned during the wheel fight.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Which the GM confirms! So these aren't just random workers — these are the same kind of creatures the Harlequins were pulling out as cannon fodder. The party's base, the Strider, is running on the labor of people who've been permanently mutated by slip exposure and trapped in debt bondage.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And that reframes everything. Every time the Strider moves, every six-second boom, that's these people working the legs. The party's home is built on exploited labor.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's a gut punch.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's a very well-constructed gut punch, yes. And then Johnny approaches the bird-like one —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Marin.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Marin. Scraggly red and blue feathers instead of hair, the beginnings of a beak. His snort comes out as a shrill sound because his nose is half-beak. Johnny offers gold for information and Marin rebuffs him. Gold is useless underground. We ain't got no use for gold.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Because Marin's debt started at two hundred gold and has grown to eighteen thousand due to interest.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Compounding interest. On a debt that can never be paid because gold is useless down here. It's a trap. It's a meat grinder. You owe two hundred, it becomes eighteen thousand, and you can never earn because you can never leave.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Marin asks — you got a ticket out of here? That's all he wants. He wants topside. He wants off the Strider.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the party can't give him that. Not right now. So Marin directs them to a forsaken sector — past acid vats and steam collection, an unlit area where people collect strange items. He's trading information for a chance, any chance, at escape.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Johnny — oh, Johnny. Johnny's negotiation in this scene is —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: A roller coaster.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's a roller coaster! He swings from Italian socialist, everyone gets sandwiches, to mob enforcer, I'll break your kneecaps, in the same breath. It's — I don't even think Johnny noticed the whiplash.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Oh, he didn't. And then the sandwich thing —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The sandwich! Johnny offers his BLT to Marin. Marin lunges for it. Benny yoinks it away. Gets a plus three sandwich yoink bonus to intimidation.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: A plus three sandwich yoink bonus. That's on the character sheet now, presumably.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Marin — Marin's response is incredible. He says, I don't know why this all of a sudden turns into aggressive posturing. He's just — he wanted the sandwich and now he's being threatened.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Johnny defuses it by promising six sandwiches daily at dawn, delivered with a note bearing Marin's name. If the note doesn't come back up, sandwiches stop and they assume he's been shanked.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's heartwarming.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's a death sentence.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's not a —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Argyle said it himself. Marin will be shanked within a week of receiving daily food deliveries. You're in a debt bondage pit where everyone is desperate and starving and you're going to send one guy six sandwiches a day with his name on a note? That's painting a target on his back in fluorescent paint.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Or — or — it's a lifeline. It's a connection to the surface. It's someone up top who knows Marin exists and cares whether he's alive. That has value.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It has value until the first person bigger than Marin decides those sandwiches should be theirs.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: ...okay. I hear you. But I choose to believe in the sandwich.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You would.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Argyle — meanwhile, Argyle is offering medical aid to the workers, right? He's checking them out. But he finds their conditions are chronic. Lifelong effects of slip exposure. Beyond his ability to treat.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is the real gut punch of that scene. Not the combat, not the politics — it's that Argyle, who wants to fix everyone, literally cannot fix this. The damage is permanent. The system that created the damage is permanent. And the party walks past it on their way to the quest objective.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They do. And that's — that's a choice, right? The game is making them choose. Do they stop and deal with this, or do they get the ink ribbon they need for the library?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They get the ink ribbon. That's the choice they make.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: For now.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: For now.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay. So they follow Marin's directions. Scaffolding over an endless pit. Dark, unlit doorway into the forsaken sector. Argyle has darkvision, the others use a flashlight —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Johnny's flashlight. Which is a nineteen-sixties-era flashlight with a switch. He keeps calling it a torch.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Because it IS a torch! A torch is a flashlight!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: In this setting it's a flashlight. And the marching order matters here — Argyle and Benny in front, Johnny behind with the light, Anzu and Othello in the rear.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the floor grate is twisted. Misshapen. Frozen in a warped form by some great twisting force. That's —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That's the Strider's structure being physically deformed. Not rusted, not worn — twisted. Something powerful did that.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And they see twinkles of light about three hundred feet ahead. Smell acrid battery acid. Hear distant voices with a melodic, sing-song quality. And Argyle —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Argyle puts in earplugs.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: To block the singing.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The mongrelfolk singing. Which, given that the voices turn out to be an evolved dialect of Urthram connected to the Sinister Six —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay, I see where you're going.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He's walking into an area where corrupted religious speech is happening and he's deafened himself to it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's a magical defense! We've seen what songs do in this world. Voidsong is a thing. The Stillness is a thing. Protecting your auditory input in a corrupted zone is smart.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's smart if you know the singing is dangerous. He doesn't. He just doesn't want to hear it. It's willful ignorance dressed up as prudence.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I think it's both. And it's in character — Argyle is the kind of guy who puts in earplugs. But then Anzu — Anzu is the one who actually hears it. And Anzu recognizes the melodic quality as resembling Urthram.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: A dead tonal language. Anzu learned it from dusty books at Belvedere.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And getting closer, it's not Urthram. It's a dialect of it. Like old English to modern English. Weird grammar, chittering undertones, sounds that feel evolved rather than preserved.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu's framing is important here. He says it's almost as if they never stopped speaking this language and it's evolved for them. That's not a dead language being recited from a book. That's a living language being spoken by a living culture.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Anzu's Urthram is dusty book Urthram. Book-learning. He can recognize it, but he can't fully access what these creatures are saying. There's a gap between scholarship and lived practice.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is a great bit of worldbuilding. The party's expert is an expert from books. The creatures in the Undercroft are speakers from birth, or from however long they've been down here. The knowledge asymmetry goes the wrong direction.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then — the perception crit. A thirty-four.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And they see them. Far more mutated than the workers near the surface. A creature with an anglerfish head. One with an atrophied face and one giant swollen eye. Another covered in porcupine quills. And one wears a horn-shaped talisman carved from Strider metal.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Carved from the same metal as the Strider itself.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Argyle's religion check — a twenty-eight — connects it to the stained glass mural of a horn-bearer seen in Tywelwyn's base.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So the same iconography. The Sinister Six. The usurper gods. It's not just present in the Undercroft — it's connected to what they've already seen topside.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the occultism check, a thirty-six, plus the religion check confirm — these creatures are unholy. Worshipping one of the Sinister Six.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And here's the thing — Anzu gets the nuanced occultism answer and Argyle gets the blunt religion answer. Anzu's is all context and theory and Argyle's is just yes, obviously, unholy.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is how those skills should work. Occultism gives you the framework, religion gives you the divine verdict. They're both right, they're just answering different questions.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Right. And then — combat.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Because Johnny tries to cast Bluff while the party is not stealthy.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They were not stealthy at all.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They were walking through a dark corridor with a flashlight. They're spotted. One of the creatures launches a fireball.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And reflex saves — Argyle and Benny fail, full damage. Johnny and Anzu succeed, half. Othello takes full twenty-three fire damage. And Johnny had Eat Fire active —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Anzu clicks his pre-cast Eat Fire, reducing fireball damage to one.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Pre-cast. Before the fireball was launched.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's either brilliant preparation or —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's metagaming. It's suspicious metagaming that the GM accepted.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I don't think it's metagaming. Anzu is a careful player. He pre-casts defensive spells in dangerous environments. That's just good play.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: He pre-cast Eat Fire in a situation where he had no specific reason to expect fire damage. He heard singing and smelled battery acid. Battery acid is not fire.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But they're in a corrupted zone worshipping the Sinister Six and he's an occultist who knows what these things can do. I think it's reasonable.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I think the GM accepted it because it's a cool moment and the table was having fun. But if I were running it, I'd at least ask why.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The GM did accept it, and then initiative is rolled, and — Argyle. Divine Wrath.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Both Oculums critically fail their saves and die instantly.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Instantly! Both of them! The two most dangerous enemies on the board, gone, just —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the bloodied Orus dies from the same blast.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: One spell, three kills, two of them on crit fails. That's — you can't plan for that. That's the dice telling a story.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Benny lands a natural twenty reaction attack for forty-seven damage on an Orus trying to fly past.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The Orus survived but barely. And Argyle gets temp hit points from Death's Call when nearby creatures die, so he's stacking benefits on top of the carnage.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: But Argyle forgot he has a reaction that deals spirit damage to attackers who hit him with piercing or slashing.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He realized it after the fight was nearly over.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is a running problem with this table. There's so much mechanical complexity that players are consistently forgetting their own abilities. It's not a knock on them — the system is dense — but it does mean the combat encounters are probably tuned for a party that's using everything, and they're using most things.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But what they are using, they're using well. Look at Johnny's turn — Dirge of Doom to frighten enemies, Haste on Benny, Benny takes an attack of opportunity for seventeen plus bleed, Johnny creates a diversion for Benny —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And then the IRS agents.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The IRS agents! Johnny summons these little IRS-agent figures that deal thirty damage and yell give us your capital gains! And the GM notes these guys don't know what capital gains are!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is funny. But the action economy question is real. Johnny spent his entire turn on a combo — Invented Vulnerability to give slashing weakness plus the summoned IRS agents — to deal thirty damage to a nearly-dead enemy.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But the slashing weakness is what enables the kill! Argyle finishes the final Orus because Johnny's weakness made it vulnerable. It's a debuff-and-burst combo. The thirty damage isn't the point. The weakness is the point.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I'll grant that. The weakness enabled the kill. But the IRS agents themselves were wasted damage on a target that was already dying. Johnny could have done the Invented Vulnerability and let Argyle clean up without spending actions on summons.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But then we don't get the capital gains line. And that line is worth more than the action economy.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That is a take.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's my take and I'm standing by it. Also — Anzu kills the last two Manus with Frostbite. Unamped Frostbite, after the amped version's save succeeded. That's efficient. That's clean.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That is clean. And then the aftermath.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The aftermath is ugly. Infernal wounds. Persistent bleed. Argyle spends multiple rounds stabilizing Benny and Johnny. He's got an item that reduces the flat check DC from twenty to ten for stopping bleeding —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Which is the kind of item you buy specifically because you've been fighting things that cause persistent bleed. Good prep.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And he uses Battle Medicine on Johnny for twenty-eight healing. And Johnny fails multiple recovery checks before finally succeeding on a DC five.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And the GM plays through multiple rounds of bleed recovery, quote, because I think it's funny.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Which — I mean, was it funny?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I think it was funny for the GM. I think the party was watching their action economy bleed out — literally — while the GM cackled. There's a difference between entertaining and punishing, and persistent bleed walks that line.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But the real revelation is — they never moved. The entire fight, the party stood on the staircase. They made it no distance at all.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They fought a whole combat without advancing a single square.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's either a testament to how dangerous the enemies were — they couldn't push forward — or a failure of tactics.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's both. The Oculums were dimension dooring around the battlefield, attacking with glaives and beards and claws, inflicting infernal fever and persistent bleed. The party was reacting, not advancing. When the biggest threats died to Divine Wrath, the remaining enemies came to them. There was no reason to move.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then the loot.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The loot is interesting. Argyle finds a non-magical horn amulet. Anzu identifies two magical pamphlets —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Perfection's First Step.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Titled Perfection's First Step. Incomplete manuscripts. About perfection, apotheosis, ascension, deliverance. Each has about six pages with the last two to three pages blank. Waiting to be completed.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And Anzu completes one in ten minutes with no apparent catch.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: No apparent catch.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But it's powered by a Sinister Six patron.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's a focus spell — Unbreaking Wave Advance — sourced from an enemy patron. There's always a catch. The catch is that you're drawing power from a usurper god. That's the catch. It's just not an overt mechanical catch right now.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Do you think the GM is going to have that come back later?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I think if you complete a spell scroll called Perfection's First Step that's about apotheosis and ascension, powered by one of the Sinister Six, and you think there's no catch, you're the mark. The catch is spiritual contamination. The catch is that the Sinister Six just felt you use their power. The catch is that something is now aware of you.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Or it's just a focus spell and the flavor is flavor.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: In this game? Nothing is just anything. That's your line, not mine.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: ...that is my line, damn it. Also — the mongrelfolk tincture.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Grows additional fingers. Plus two reflex DC, twenty-foot climb speed for ten minutes. And it is, quote, gritty and spicy.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Gritty and spicy! I love that. I love that the mongrelfolk have their own alchemy. These aren't just suffering workers — they have a culture, they have craft, they have stuff that the party can't make.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Agreed. That's good worldbuilding. The mongrelfolk aren't just victims. They have agency and tools. Limited, but real.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And then Argyle swaps out Show the Way for Locate, targeting ink ribbon, and —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: After an extended rules debate with the GM about what Show the Way actually does.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It says AND, not TO!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That's the kind of pedantic spell-text argument that splits tables. But they resolve it, Argyle gets Locate, it points north, and they navigate to a barracks room.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Full of tightly stacked metal beds, no mattresses, twisted frames from oversized occupants. Overwhelming acid smell. More wall art. And Detect Magic reveals a level five magic object in a pack.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Inside — the ink ribbon. A film-reel container, deep red. Plus rags, a bar of lye, and a small key with a skull emblazoned on it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The skull key! That's a Chekhov's gun if I've ever seen one.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Anzu finds a parchment with runic markings related to but not quite Urthram. So there's another layer of text they can't fully read. More knowledge they can't access.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But the ink ribbon — they got it. The primary quest objective. They can go back to the bone-faced curator and get library access.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They can. But they don't go back. They push forward.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They push forward! Because Anzu — Anzu compares the music notes on the walls to their own voidsong paper.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And this is where it gets really interesting. The notation uses a different scale, but the actual tones described are a pretty good match. The Sinister Six are emulating voidsong.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The same power Anzu wields. The same thing that carved itself into Anzu's soul. The Sinister Six are trying to replicate it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Anzu says — they've kind of figured out how to — and then trails off. Doesn't finish the thought. Because the implications are terrifying.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So is this about Anzu specifically? Are the Sinister Six copying Anzu's power?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I don't think so. I think voidsong is a broader cosmic phenomenon. The Sinister Six are tapping into the same source that the voidsong came from. Anzu is a vessel for it. The Sinister Six are trying to build their own vessels, their own versions. It's not about Anzu personally — it's about the power.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But that still means Anzu is connected to the enemy whether they like it or not. They're all drinking from the same well.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Exactly. And the wall art reinforces it — poems about perfection, apotheosis, ascension, deliverance. Crude drawings of stick figures dancing around an orb. Extensive horn iconography. The Sinister Six's worship isn't just ritual — it's an attempt to replicate a specific cosmic power. And the party's own occultist carries that power in their soul.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: That's — that's a heavy thread.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's the heaviest thread of the session.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay. And then — the end. They push forward past the ink ribbon, into increasingly dense spider webs, cramped acid-smelling hallways, skittering sounds beneath the walls.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Johnny's perception crit lets him guide the party through the webs. Cancels Anzu's failure. Argyle and Johnny both crit their stealth and acrobatics. After fifteen minutes of careful navigation —

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: They feel a tingle. Like passing through an air curtain. They've entered a Fane.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: A Fane of the Sinister Six. Inside the Strider. Their base. Their home. The thing they've been fortifying with walls and moats and Oil Slicked Walls — it contains an enemy stronghold.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And the session ends. Right there. On the threshold.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: With depleted big spells and an infernal-fever-infected Johnny.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: And you think they should have retreated.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I think pressing into a Fane with Argyle's Divine Wrath already spent, with Johnny running persistent bleed from infernal wounds, with no idea what's inside — I think that's foolhardy.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Or it's brave. They have momentum. They've just won a fight. They've found the quest objective. They've discovered the Sinister Six are emulating voidsong. They're on a roll —

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They're on a roll into a desecrated zone that they know nothing about. Fanes are where hearts live. Hearts have control over their fanes. They can make them look like whatever they want. The party is walking into someone else's domain at half strength.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: But they don't know it's a Fane until they feel the tingle. By then they're through the air curtain. Retreating means turning your back on whatever's inside.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Retreating means living to come back at full strength.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Retreating means giving the enemy time to prepare, to reinforce, to notice you were there. You push through when you have the chance.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You push through when you have the resources. They don't.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We'll find out next session.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: We will. And I suspect we'll find out the hard way.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: ...you might be right.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: I usually am.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Don't push it.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The spider webs, the skittering — something's in there. Something big. And they walked in with a fever and empty spell slots.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Well — you had to be there.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: We were there.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I know. I'm just saying — next session's going to be something.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It certainly is.

episodes.title: The Canary in the Undercroft

A.name: Bram
A.persona: warm, boisterous, fluent but imprecise; the storyteller who relives the best moments with relish and happily embellishes. Talks in long, rolling run-on sentences that pile clause on clause; makes big sweeping claims he then has to walk back; reliably gets a name, number, or detail wrong and gets corrected (usually by Maeve); now and then runs clean out of sentence and lands on a shrug like "you... you had to be there." Drives the recap forward and overshoots

B.name: Maeve
B.persona: warm and dry, precise but pointed; the long-time regular whose knowledge of the setting is lived rather than studied. Lands the exact word, name, or date the others fumble for and reins Bram in with a flat one-line correction — she finishes her sentences and finishes them short. But she's not only the fact-checker: she needles, too, pushing on WHY the characters did what they did and making Bram defend his reads, poking at the table's heroics and at sentiment with a wink. Grounds events in how the world actually works; the only one reliably right, so let her be plainly wrong exactly once so she isn't an oracle

episodes.synopsis: Team Anzu presses deeper into the Strider's Undercroft, navigating warped hallways and a chamber of roaring pistons before sneaking past curtains of spider silk draped across a colossal shaft. Beyond, they discover an ancient shrine lined with statues of Aurelia the First's original crusading party, raising troubling questions about whether a Heart's Fane has been co-opted by something lurking in the dark. When massive sword-armed spiders and a potion-thieving apothecary bug descend, the Heartbreakers must burn through their last spell slots to survive, ending bloodied and depleted at the foot of unfamiliar stairs.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: —and look, I'm just saying, Team Anzu is a fine name, it's a fine working title, and Johnny was being dramatic about it—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's a bad name, Bram. It's a bad name and you know it. Benny said Heartbreakers right there at the top of the session and everyone just — fumbled past it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Heartbreakers is good, I'll give you that, Heartbreakers has swagger, but you can't just — you can't name your faction after your bit, Maeve, that's not how you build a brand, you gotta earn it first, and they hadn't even killed a heart yet at that point — well, no, they'd killed Whirling in Rags, but that was—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They'd killed Whirling in Rags the previous session. They'd harvested two hearts. They'd earned it.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Okay, fine, but you know what, that's not the point, the point is they went down into the Undercroft and they went down HARD, like, this was a proper dungeon crawl, and we haven't seen these guys do a real dungeon crawl yet, and it was — I mean, Johnny's recap at the top was beautiful, right, just this breathless — "we met Maranthorn, we paid him in sandwiches"—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They paid a debt-enslaved mongrel folk worker in sandwiches.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: In sandwiches! Daily sandwich deliveries! And it was — okay, it was maybe not the most airtight promise they've ever made, but it got them past the mongrel folk, it got them into the forsaken sector, and then Argyle just — lights up. Divine Wrath, holy water, the whole nine yards, just obliterates the Sinister Six cultists in what, one turn?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The Oculums and the Oris creatures, yes. And that was a genuine turning point, I'll grant you. Argyle's Holy Water plus Divine Wrath crit-killed both Oculums and an Orus in a single round. That's not nothing.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's not nothing, it's everything! That's the whole combat right there! And that's why they kept going, that's the whole reason they pushed deeper, because when your champion just nukes an encounter off the board, you feel invincible, you feel like—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: You feel reckless. That's what you feel. And that's exactly what happened.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: No, no, no, that's not — okay, look, they found the ink ribbon, they found the manuscripts, they found the skull key, they got what they came for, they could've turned around, but they didn't, and I think that's the right call because — and this is the thing nobody's talking about — they're already in a Fane. They crossed that threshold last session. They passed through the air curtain. They're IN it. You don't turn around when you're in a Fane, you push forward and you find the heart, because the heart is the whole point.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: The heart is the whole point if you have the resources to take it. Which, by the end of this session, they manifestly did not. But we'll get there. Let's talk about the piston room first, because that's where the resource bleeding starts.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The piston room! Oh, the piston room was incredible, just this — imagine it, right, you're in this warped hallway deep in the guts of the Strider, the walls are twisting, the floor is tilted, you're leaning rightward, and then you come out into this enormous cylindrical chamber, eight massive pistons crisscrossing back and forth, slamming into the ceiling, and the whole thing is just covered in spider webbing, floor to ceiling—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And Benny falls through the floor.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Benny falls through the floor! Just — whoops, no floor! And he catches himself, barely, and he's spooked like a cat, and it's — it was funny, it was a great moment, but it also tells you something about this place, right, the architecture itself is compromised, the Undercroft is not what they were told it was, Josh made a point of saying this is not new construction, this is old, this is warped—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Right, and that's a significant lore beat, actually. Josh explicitly said there's no way the Undercroft got to the state it's in within six months. So the Strider was not freshly built. Whatever it is, it's old, or it's built on something old. And then Anzu — actually, it was Anzu who noticed, right, that the Fane looks like the Strider. The Fane's structure mirrors the Strider's structure. Which raises the question—

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Which raises the GREAT question, the best question of the night, which is: can a heart get co-opted? And Johnny asks it, right, he's like, can Big Bug come in and just — take over a heart? And Anzu rolls, what was it, a thirty-eight on occultism with Johnny aiding—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Johnny's aid was a forty-one, which is — yes, it was a crit on the aid, Anzu's own roll was high, and the total was a thirty-eight, which also crit'd. And what Josh gave them was genuinely important lore: yes, a heart can be co-opted by something more powerful. You can't force it against its will directly — mind control doesn't work on hearts — but you can coerce it. You can, and I'm quoting the spirit of what Josh said here, push the right levers. And the Fane's structure stays in the image the heart produced, even if the heart is being made to do something else.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: So Big Bug — and I love that they just started calling it Big Bug, that's beautiful, that's pure table energy — Big Bug could have come in and muscled this heart into doing something for the spiders instead of for the Strider. And that's — I mean, that's a huge reveal, because it means the hearts aren't these sacrosanct things, they're not untouchable, they can be dominated, or coerced, or—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Not dominated. Coerced. There's a difference, and Josh was careful about it. You can't mind-control a heart. But you can apply pressure. And that's — look, we don't know what's actually happening with this particular heart yet. We don't know if it's been co-opted. We know the Fane looks like the Strider, we know there are spiders everywhere, and we know the linkages — the mechanical linkages in the Strider's guts — have been gummed up by webbing in places. That's circumstantial.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: It's pretty damn convincing circumstantial! The webs are everywhere, the spiders are everywhere, the machinery is being choked—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Some of the machinery. Josh was clear that the pistons in that room were still functioning. Some linkages were gummed up, others weren't. So it's not a total takeover, if it is one. It's partial.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Fine, partial, but — okay, here's where I want to push on you, because you said the resource bleeding starts in the piston room, and I think that's unfair, because what happened in the piston room is they had a problem — hundred-foot gap, pistons in the way, webs on the walls — and they solved it. Anzu cast Fly on Argyle, Anzu cast Levitate on Benny, Johnny Dimension Doored across, and they just — they flew over. Problem solved. No damage, no combat, clean.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They burned a third-rank spell and a fourth-rank spell. Fly and Levitate. And then Johnny burned a Dimension Door. That's three spell slots to cross a room they didn't need to cross. They could have turned back.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Turned back to what? They're in a Fane! If they turn back, they've still got to navigate a quarter mile of webbed hallway to get out, and they haven't found the heart yet—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They could have turned back, rested, come back with a better plan. Instead they pushed forward into unknown territory with diminishing resources, and that is the story of this entire session. Every decision after this point is downstream of that choice.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: I just — I can't agree with that, because the whole point of a dungeon crawl is that you push until you can't push anymore, and then you rest in the dungeon, that's — that's classic, that's how it works—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: That's how it works when you have a safe place to rest. Which they didn't. And don't have. Still don't.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: We'll come back to that. But first — the piston room crossing, Johnny goes first, he Dimension Doors across, he does a perception check, a thirty-one, which is good but not amazing, Josh makes him roll a d-two, a literal coin flip, for whether there's a button or switch on the other side—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: And he lost the coin flip.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: He lost the coin flip! And Johnny's reaction, just — "no, that's the bad one!" — it was perfect, it was this beautiful moment of — of the dice giveth and the dice taketh away, because he rolled well enough to get the perception check but then the coin flip just—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: It's a funny moment, but it also means they crossed the room, burned those spells, and got nothing for it. No switch, no shortcut, no way to turn off the pistons. Just a doorway deeper in.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: A doorway deeper in, which is what they wanted! They wanted to go deeper in! That's the whole point!

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Fine. Let's talk about what they found deeper in, then.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: The silk curtain room. Oh, this was — this was gorgeous, right, this enormous cylindrical shaft, like an old elevator shaft that's been commandeered, rafters crossing at different angles, and from the ceiling, just thousands and thousands of strands of spider silk, hanging down like curtains, and in among the silk you can see these blue-black figures moving, and these nodules, these silk-wrapped shapes—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: Egg sacs, presumably.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Presumably! And Benny, because he's in front, because they gave him the Obsidian Goggles and sent him in as the canary—

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.name: Maeve
transcript.text: They literally called him a canary. They painted him yellow in their heads.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.name: Bram
transcript.text: Because it's funny!
